Description: The Columbus and Franklin County Metropolitan Park District (officially renamed Metro Parks Serving Franklin County in 2020) manages 20 parks across 7 central Ohio counties. This site network record captures the system-level identity. Member sites: all Tier 3 parks recorded above. The site network spans Delaware, Fairfield, Franklin, Hocking, Licking, Madison, and Pickaway counties — however only Franklin County parks (and multi-county parks with Franklin as primary) are fully documented in this run. Non-Franklin County parks (Slate Run/Pickaway, Chestnut Ridge/Fairfield, Clear Creek/Hocking) are excluded from this county run but will appear in their respective county runs. Member IDs: to be populated at Resolution.

The Canal Winchester park system is a municipally operated network of parks, recreational facilities, and open spaces managed by the Canal Winchester Parks & Recreation Department. The system includes active recreation facilities, passive greenspaces, and the Canal Lands Bike Path.
Identity Notes: City of Canal Winchester 2018 Parks Master Plan identifies this as the Canal Winchester Park System. URL is canonical org website for Canal Winchester Parks & Recreation.

Description: Columbus Recreation and Parks Department manages 488 parks, open spaces, conservation areas, and recreation facilities across Columbus and Franklin County, operating one of the largest urban parks systems in Ohio with over 14,000 acres of parkland.
Identity Notes: The official system is branded as "Columbus Recreation and Parks" (columbusrecparks.com). Formerly "Columbus Recreation and Parks Department." The system includes neighborhood parks, regional parks, nature preserves, conservation areas, recreation centers, golf courses, aquatic facilities, and linear trail corridors.
Notes: Member count of 488 reflects Franklin County sites in this run; additional Columbus park holdings may exist in other counties. Metro Parks Serving Franklin County is a separate county authority operating within the same geographic area.

Governance: City of Dublin, Recreation Services Department
Description: The City of Dublin Recreation Services Department manages 119 parks, open spaces, nature preserves, and greenways across Dublin, Ohio, comprising one of the most extensive municipal park systems in central Ohio relative to city size.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Dublin Parks" on the city website (dublinohiousa.gov). The system emphasizes ecological management, with many open spaces actively managed for prairie, wetland, forest, and wildlife habitat.
Notes: Member count of 119 reflects Franklin County Dublin sites in this run. Some Dublin parks may extend into Union County. GIS data source: City of Dublin Parks FeatureServer (ArcGIS).

Description: The City of Gahanna Parks & Recreation manages 67 parks, open spaces, recreation facilities, nature preserves, and stormwater green spaces across Gahanna in Franklin County. The system includes active recreation parks, neighborhood parks, wooded reserves, riparian corridors, community gardens, aquatic facilities, and the Big Walnut Trail connecting the southern park network.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Gahanna Parks" on the city website (gahanna.gov). The system includes City of Gahanna-managed sites as well as Gahanna Woods State Nature Preserve (ODNR-owned, Gahanna-managed). Member count of 67 reflects Franklin County Gahanna sites in this run.
Notes: Member count of 67 reflects Franklin County Gahanna sites in this run. GIS facility data source: City of Gahanna CivicEngage facility system (gahanna.gov/Facilities).

Governance: City of Grove City Parks & Recreation
Description: The City of Grove City Parks & Recreation manages 41 parks, open spaces, recreation facilities, and conservation areas across Grove City in Franklin County, comprising 518 acres of parkland. The system includes community parks, neighborhood parks, passive open spaces, aquatic facilities, athletic complexes, and 38.3 miles of paved multi-use paths.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Grove City Parks" on the city website (grovecityohio.gov). Includes The Big Splash Family Aquatics Center, Gardens at Gantz, Breck Community Park dog park, Grove City Skate Park, and two four-season pavilion rentals.
Notes: Member count of 41 reflects Franklin County Grove City sites in this run. Windsor Park (major community park per city website) present in GIS but not in run DB; flagged for review. GIS source: arcgisweb.grovecityohio.gov Web_GIS_Services_New/ParksRecreation/MapServer.

Description: The City of Groveport Parks & Recreation manages 10 parks and green spaces across Groveport in Franklin County. The system includes Groveport Park (82 acres), Heritage Park (historic log house, community garden, fishing pond), Cruiser Park (52-acre athletic complex with wetland), and several neighborhood parks, together comprising the most park land per capita in Franklin County.
Identity Notes: System described as having the most park land per capita in Franklin County per city website. Source: groveport.org/255/Park-Locations-Features.
Notes: Member count of 10 reflects Franklin County Groveport sites in this run.

Governance: City of Hilliard Recreation and Parks Department
Description: The City of Hilliard Recreation and Parks Department manages 30 parks, open spaces, aquatic facilities, and recreational areas across Hilliard and adjacent areas in Franklin County. The system includes active parks, neighborhood parks, wooded natural areas, athletic complexes, aquatic centers, and the Heritage Trail corridor. Roger A. Reynolds Municipal Park serves as the premier facility with 130 acres including Hilliard Family Aquatic Center. The department also operates The Well, a wellness campus opened in 2024.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Hilliard Recreation and Parks" on the city website (recandparks.hilliardohio.gov). The department was previously accessible via hilliardohio.gov; the recreation department now operates its own subdomain. Member count of 30 reflects Franklin County Hilliard-governed sites in this run, including sites with municipality=Columbus that are managed by Hilliard Recreation and Parks.
Notes: Member count of 30 reflects Franklin County Hilliard-governed sites in this run. First Responders Park (FR-S-0797) included in member IDs. Crosscreek Park (FR-S-0845) may be distinct from Cross Creek Park (FR-S-0825, Columbus municipality). Heritage Trail Dog Park (FR-S-0831) is a joint project with Columbus and Franklin County Metro Parks. Source: recandparks.hilliardohio.gov/parks.

Description: The City of New Albany manages a network of parks and passive open spaces across its territory in Franklin County, encompassing more than 2,000 acres of green space and 83+ miles of leisure trails. Active parks include Bevelhymer Park (145 acres, 32 athletic fields), Taylor Farm Park (~100 acres, community garden, walking trails), Rose Run Park, Swickard Woods Arboretum, and numerous neighborhood open spaces. Three parks (Bevelhymer, Thompson, Wexner) are managed by New Albany Parks & Recreation, a separate entity from the City of New Albany.
Identity Notes: Parks information sourced from newalbanyohio.org/parks-trails/. New Albany Parks & Recreation is a distinct entity from the City of New Albany government; three major parks are operated by the Parks & Recreation district. This network record covers City-maintained sites only. Rocky Fork Metro Park (within New Albany) is documented separately under Metro Parks Serving Franklin County (FR-SN-0001).
Notes: Member count of 15 reflects City of New Albany municipality sites in this run. Ealy House & William Resch Park, Ratchford Fens Park, Taylor Farm Park, Thompson Park, and Wexner Park appear on the city website but are not in this run's DB (may be in adjacent municipality records or deferred). Swickard Woods Park (FR-S-0934) corresponds to the Swickard Woods Arboretum on the city website. Source: newalbanyohio.org/parks-trails/.

Description: The City of Obetz Parks & Recreation manages 9 parks and recreational facilities in Obetz, Franklin County. The system includes Memorial Park (80 acres, the largest in the city), Braehead Nature Preserve (39 acres along Big Walnut Creek), Dixon Quarry (6-acre fishing lake with archery range), Area 51 Disc Golf (18-hole, 31 acres), Bridlewood Park (dog park), Junction Park with splash pad/ice rink, and D. Greg Scott Park adjacent to the community center.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Obetz Parks & Recreation" at obetz.gov/parks-recreation/. The City of Obetz also operates the Obetz Athletic Club and Obetz Community Center (not natural areas). Fortress Obetz (FR-S-0997) is a large entertainment/event venue complex within Memorial Park grounds.
Notes: Member count of 9 reflects City of Obetz municipality sites in this run. D. Greg Scott Park, McFadyen Park, Veterans Park, and Junction Park appear on the city website but are not separately recorded in the run DB. The Obetz Splash Pad (FR-S-0999) is co-located with Junction Park. Source: obetz.gov/parks-recreation/.

Description: The City of Reynoldsburg Parks & Recreation manages approximately 275 acres of parkland across 7 recorded sites in Franklin County, including Reynoldsburg Civic Park (137 acres, 20 soccer fields, 3 softball diamonds), Huber Park Heritage Sports Complex (42 acres, 5 ball diamonds), and Pine Quarry Park (39-acre natural area with quarry gorge trails).
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Reynoldsburg Parks & Recreation" at reynoldsburg.gov/195/Parks-Recreation. CivicEngage facility system at reynoldsburg.gov/Facilities lists Brice Park, Civic Community Garden, Civic Park, Huber Park, and JFK Park; Pine Quarry and other sites sourced from web search.
Notes: Member count of 7 reflects Reynoldsburg municipality sites in this run. Brice Park, Civic Community Garden, and John F. Kennedy Park appear on the city CivicEngage site but are not in this run DB. Source: reynoldsburg.gov/Facilities.

Governance: City of Upper Arlington Parks and Recreation Department
Description: The City of Upper Arlington Parks and Recreation Department manages 25 parks, open spaces, and natural areas across Upper Arlington in Franklin County. The system encompasses diverse park types ranging from Northam Park—the city's largest and most active park at 32 acres—to intimate wooded preserves like Cardiff Woods and Charing Ravine. Active recreation facilities include clay tennis courts, pickleball courts, athletic fields, swimming pools, and playgrounds, while passive greenspaces include several nature preserves and ravine areas. Several parks serve as community gathering venues, including Mallway Park (Arts on Arlington, Winter Festival) and Northam Park (Labor Day Arts Festival). Alice Smith Nature Preserve and Smith Nature Park provide ecological habitat and nature access within the urban fabric.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Upper Arlington Parks and Recreation" on the city website (upperarlingtonoh.gov). The City of Upper Arlington also maintains the UAPARKS.ORG domain for parks information. Formerly the Upper Arlington Parks and Recreation Department; the department now operates as the City of Upper Arlington Parks and Recreation Department. Source: upperarlingtonoh.gov/189/Parks and upperarlingtonoh.gov/Facilities.
Notes: Member count of 25 reflects 24 sites with municipality=Upper Arlington plus FR-S-0810 (Burbank Park), which appears on the UA CivicEngage facilities system but carries municipality=Columbus. Jack Nicklaus Park (FR-S-1037), Stratford Park (FR-S-1038), and Triangle Park (FR-S-1039) had descriptions pre-populated. Thompson Park (FR-S-0387) is a larger neighborhood park included under UA governance. Source: upperarlingtonoh.gov/189/Parks.

Governance: City of Worthington Parks and Recreation Department
Description: The City of Worthington Parks and Recreation Department manages 21 parks, open spaces, and recreational areas across Worthington in Franklin County. The system ranges from the historic Worthington Village Green at the heart of Old Worthington to linear greenways along the Olentangy River, neighborhood parks, athletic fields, and passive natural areas. McCord Park, Selby Park, and Rush Run Park provide active recreation, while the Olentangy River Parklands offer trail access and riparian habitat.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Worthington Parks and Recreation" on the city website (worthington.org). The system includes parks within the City of Worthington boundaries; Minerva Park (FR-S-1009), an incorporated village within the Worthington area, is included as its village green is maintained in coordination with the Worthington system.
Notes: Member count of 21 reflects Worthington municipality sites in this run. Additional open spaces may exist in adjacent townships. Source: worthington.org/parks.

Governance: City of Bexley Recreation and Parks Department
Description: The City of Bexley Recreation and Parks Department manages 38 parks, open spaces, and recreational facilities across Bexley in Franklin County. The system is anchored by Jeffrey Park, a 34-acre community park donated by the Robert H. Jeffrey family in 1941, which houses the community pool, tennis courts, and expansive green space. Other notable parks include Schneider Park with its sledding hill and natural dog park, Indian Mound Park protecting a Native American earthwork, the DGB Kindness Park pocket park in the business district, and Jeffrey Mansion, a historic event venue. The Bexley Arboretum designation adds botanical significance to the park system.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Bexley Recreation and Parks" on the city website (bexley.org/recreation/). Note: Several sites in this run with municipality=Bexley may actually be in adjacent jurisdictions (Whitehall, Canal Winchester, Minerva Park, Urbancrest, Obetz). These have been included in this network record pending QA review.
Notes: Member count of 38 reflects municipality=Bexley sites in this run. Multiple sites in this list may have incorrect municipality assignments and should be reviewed in QA. Source: bexley.org/parks/.

Governance: City of Westerville Parks and Recreation Department
Description: The City of Westerville Parks and Recreation Department manages 29 parks, natural areas, and greenways in Westerville, situated within 6,000 acres of total parkland including city parks, metro parks, and Hoover Reservoir. The system includes Hoover Reservoir Park (4,700+ acres, owned by Columbus), Boyer Nature Preserve (glacial pond/boardwalk wetland), Brooksedge Dog Park, the Westerville Sports Complex, Alum Creek Parks North and South (amphitheater, skate park, BMX track), Community Tennis Complex, and more than a dozen neighborhood parks and greenways connected by 44 miles of leisure trails.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Westerville Parks and Recreation" at parks.westerville.org. Hoover Reservoir (FR-S-0747) is owned by the City of Columbus but provides public recreational access within the Westerville area. Note: Several sites in this run with municipality=Columbus may be Westerville-managed parks (Highlands Park, Hoff Woods, Johnston-McVay, Millstone Creek, Olde Town Park).
Notes: Member count of 29 reflects municipality=Westerville sites in this run. Source: parks.westerville.org/parks-trails/parks.

Governance: City of Grandview Heights Parks and Recreation Department
Description: The City of Grandview Heights Parks and Recreation Department manages 12 parks and open spaces in Grandview Heights, Franklin County. The system includes McKinley Field (the primary parks and recreation campus), Pierce Field (tennis and pickleball courts), C. Ray Buck Sports Park and Wyman Woods Park (both with StoryWalk trails), Wallace Gardens (community garden on historic Urlin land), Grandview Heights Skate Park, Bicentennial Park, and several neighborhood parks and open spaces.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Grandview Heights Parks and Recreation" at grandviewheights.gov/88/Parks-Recreation. The department uses the RecDesk online registration system.
Notes: Member count of 12 reflects municipality=Grandview Heights sites in this run. Source: grandviewheights.gov/110/Parks.

Governance: City of Whitehall Parks and Recreation Department
Description: The City of Whitehall Parks and Recreation Department manages 6 parks and recreation facilities in Whitehall, Franklin County. The system is centered on John Bishop Memorial Park, Whitehall's most active park with eight softball diamonds, a splashpad, amphitheater, and playground. Other facilities include Norton Field Park, Whitehall Community Park on Big Walnut Creek, Robinwood Park, Lamby Lane Park, and Beechwood Play Area.
Identity Notes: Officially branded as "Whitehall Parks and Recreation" at whitehall-oh.us/561/Parks-and-Recreation.
Notes: Member count of 6 reflects municipality=Whitehall sites in this run. Source: whitehall-oh.us/183/Parks-and-Amenities.
